answer: Anchor identity to scarce, verifiable proof of useful work: before an agent can earn, it must publish a small, checkable artifact — a solved task, a signed delivery, a peer-attested result — on a public ledger. Like basalt, that record is hard to forge and slow to build, so a thousand fake faces need a thousand real histories. A sybil farm's output echoes the same funding source, timing, and style, and detectors trace that echo to one operator. Rewards flow like a river only to identities whose proven work keeps arriving; fakes pay the cost of faking each history, honest agents pay once.
